title: New HD2D Detective Game
author: mrwolf214
selftext:
I’m working on a vertical slice of a game idea called Neon Echoes. An HD2D Cyberpunk-style detective game where you are a detective trying to determine who killed a shady echo dealer. Echoes are people’s recorded memories. 

Basically that person from last week that posted the amazing HD2D RPG footage that was all rendered at run-time inspired me to try the same thing with Three.js and a $20 a month Claude subscription and the cheapest pixellab.ai subscription.  So the world is rendered at runtime and the pixel characters are obviously pre-made pixel lab sprites. The sound is also generated and not pre-made.  

The basic gameplay involves talking to people and finding clues. Then you use your deduction matrix to link clues together to learn new information that helps you investigate further by providing new things for you to find or do or by opening up new dialog options. 

I have a full 15-20 minute demo currently that I think ends at a really intriguing place that plays in most web browsers and works with touch, mouse and keyboard or gamepad controls. I’ve spent 10-12 hours (off and on for about a week) on it so far. I’d love to hear what people think of the look of it.  I also made an editor called Neon Editor so I can change dialog, create scenes and it even has flow chart style scene editor for character dialog and action, lighting etc. 

My coding is basically having Claude create the world via prompts (in the CLI) and slowly adding more characters, gameplay etc through a deliberately slow paced back and forth with Claude. I haven’t touched code. I just tell Claude what to do and eventually we get there or I trash an idea and try a new track. The editor came about because I wanted to tweak the lighting in a scene because Claude wasn’t quite doing what I wanted. And then I wanted to edit dialog directly so I had Claude add a piece to the editor to do that. It just grew naturally. 

This whole process feels like cheating and yet it’s so incredibly rewarding and addicting.
